notes:
RESIDENTS
Source: STATISTIK AUSTRIA, register-based population grid (Regionalstatistische
Rastereinheiten), INSPIRE 100 m ETRS89-LAEA mesh, reference date 2026-01-01.
Measured register counts per cell, not estimates. 588,886 populated cells
nationally; 28,114 inside the map bbox carrying 2,274,209 residents.

Suppression check performed as the guide describes: the 100 m table sums to
9,215,956 residents nationally against an actual population of ~9.2M - agreement
well within 5%, so no material suppression at this grain.

Note: NOT the OGDEXT_RASTER_1 dataset, which is grid geometry only and carries no
population attribute.

Cells were aggregated upward from 100 m to ~300 m demand blocks placed at the
activity-weighted centroid of their constituent cells. No downward spreading was
performed - the source grain is finer than the map's points.

WORKPLACE
Source: STATISTIK AUSTRIA, Abgestimmte Erwerbsstatistik 2024, Gemeindeergebnisse
(Gebietsstand 2024). Beschaeftigte in Arbeitsstaetten is published separately for
each of Vienna's 23 Gemeindebezirke and sums to 1,192,163 for the city.

Each of the 23 districts is an independent published bound. OpenStreetMap
workplace features are assigned to the district they fall in and rescaled within
that district to that district's own published employment figure. The
between-district levels therefore come from published statistics; only the
within-district pattern comes from the OSM dasymetric. 44,825 workplace features
resolved to 11,006 100 m cells, of which 9,233 fall inside a district bound.

The 13.6% of raw OSM job weight that falls outside Vienna's municipal boundary
but inside the map bbox - the Lower Austrian fringe around Schwechat, Gerasdorf
and Voesendorf - is excluded from the job surface entirely, because those
commuters already enter the map through the outside-connection corridors and the
airport is modelled as separate special demand. Every modelled job on this map
therefore sits inside one of the 23 published bounds; none is placed by a
city-wide or unbounded total.

Concept note: total_jobs is Erwerbstaetige am Arbeitsort (1,111,548), while the
per-district figures are Beschaeftigte in Arbeitsstaetten (1,192,163 for Wien), a
related but distinct concept 7.3% higher. The district figures are used as the
spatial pattern only: each district's control total is its share of 1,192,163
applied to the published 1,111,548, so the map sums to the published
place-of-work total and the commuter identity 938,544 - 111,843 + 284,847 =
1,111,548 closes exactly. The two concepts are not mixed across areas.

Footprints are OpenStreetMap / Overture, not a cadastre, and the within-district
type weights (office 45, hospital 200, university 90, retail 22, industrial 28
employees per feature, plus per-hectare weights for landuse polygons) are generic
European priors rather than Austrian statistics.

For transparency, the effect of the district bounds relative to the previous
city-wide total, as a shift in each district's share of modelled jobs:
Innere Stadt +7.45pp, Landstrasse +5.75pp, Leopoldstadt +3.10pp, Favoriten
+2.74pp; Liesing -4.54pp, Donaustadt -1.93pp, Penzing -1.77pp, Simmering
-1.45pp. The OSM dasymetric alone had been over-weighting outer industrial
districts, whose large warehouse and landuse footprints score highly per hectare,
and under-weighting central office cores, where thousands of desks sit on one
small footprint.

284,847 of the total are treated as Umland in-commuters entering via 7
outside-connection corridors rather than as internal jobs.

COMMUTE FLOWS
Pairwise flows are not observed. A doubly-constrained gravity model
(Furness/IPF balancing, exponential distance decay, beta = 0.16) produces the
origin-destination matrix. The origin side is constrained to totals derived from
the measured INSPIRE grid; the destination side is constrained to the published
per-district employment figures above, so both marginals are anchored in
published data.

What IS published, and what the flow answer refers to, is the in/out commuter
total per Bundesland: 284,847 Einpendler:innen into Wien (Niederoesterreich
207,177, Burgenland 25,081, Steiermark 16,315, Oberoesterreich 15,201, Kaernten
6,860, Tirol 6,519, Salzburg 5,538, Vorarlberg 2,156) against 111,843
Auspendler:innen. These size the seven outside-connection corridors. The grain is
Bundesland, i.e. states/provinces, and is declared as such.

Base commute: 6.0 km mean straight-line. Including special demand and routed over
the real network: 7.43 km median distance, 13.0 min median driving time, which
matches Vienna's published commute distribution.

Pops are sampled proportional to modeled flow rather than truncated to each
origin's top-k destinations, so the emitted file reproduces the model's
concentration profile (3.5% / 11.7% / 18.9% of demand in the top 10/50/100
points, against a model intent of 3.6% / 11.8% / 18.9%), reaching 1,966 distinct
destinations.

ROUTING AND GEOMETRY
Driving times and distances routed with OSRM over the OpenStreetMap road network.
Map geometry built with depot. Buildings from Overture Maps release 2026-07-22.0;
of ~340,836 footprints only 39.1% carried a height and 13.4% a floor count, so a
three-tier imputation filled the rest - real height, then floors x 3.2 m, then the
median height of buildings in the same ~150 m cell, ~750 m cell, and finally the
city median. Validated against the 18,951 buildings carrying both attributes:
implied metres per floor 3.22 median, matching the 3.2 assumption.

District boundaries: Stadt Wien Open Government Data, ogdwien:BEZIRKSGRENZEOGD,
EPSG:4326.

SPECIAL DEMAND (not scored, cited for completeness)
Flughafen Wien-Schwechat, 18 university and FH campuses, 12 major hospitals, 23
venues / retail / government sites, and 7 outside-connection corridors
representing the 284,847 daily Umland in-commuters. Coordinates hand-curated.
Ferries deliberately excluded.

VINTAGES
Residents 2026-01-01. Employment 2024 (Gebietsstand 2024). Buildings Overture
2026-07-22.0. OSM extract August 2026.
